lines: Two hundred thousand years ago, our species lives only in Africa. Neanderthals and Denisovans live in Eurasia.
Each colour of sand is a strand of ancestry.
Some groups leave Africa early, about a hundred and twenty thousand years ago, but leave little trace today.
Then, between seventy and fifty thousand years ago, a small band crosses out of Africa.
They spread fast, along the coasts to South Asia, and by boat to Australia.
Along the way they mix with Neanderthals. People outside Africa carry about two percent Neanderthal DNA, and many Africans carry a smaller trace.
In Island Southeast Asia, they meet Denisovans.
People reach Europe and East Asia. Our cousins disappear, but a little of their sand lives on in us.
Long apart, each region's sand drifts into its own colour.
At least twenty thousand years ago, a few founders cross into the Americas.
A handful of grains seeds two continents: the founder effect.
About eleven thousand years ago, farming begins in the Fertile Crescent, and independently elsewhere. Farmers spread, and mix with the foragers they meet.
Herders from the steppe sweep into Europe and South Asia.
The Bantu expansion carries West-Central African ancestry across half a continent.
Austronesian sailors from Taiwan cross two oceans...
...to Polynesia, and to Madagascar, where Asian and African ancestry meet.
By fifteen hundred, ships link every continent, and the Americas are transformed by conquest, disease and the transatlantic slave trade.
Settlers transform Australia, Siberia and southern Africa.
Modern migration keeps stirring the sand, and people gather in cities.
Today, almost every vessel holds sand from many places. Yet islands of ancestry endure, from New Guinea to the Andes.
And underneath... it was always the same sand. Every person alive descends from those first African grains.
